environment.method_note: gdb/ptrace is unavailable under qemu on this host; verification uses compiled-in ASan evidence (Tier A asan_reproduce) and patch differential (Tier A patch_differential). Tier-B line coverage of intermediate lines needs a native amd64 rebuild and is recorded as deferred.

R1_parser_admitted.evidence: Frame #4 of the ASan allocation stack in the vul reproduction is processSecureChannelMessage ua_server_binary.c:628; the message cleared SecureChannel framing and entered MSG dispatch.

line_coverage.reason: processMSG is witnessed via ASan allocation frame #3 (ua_server_binary.c:458); exact-line coverage of the decode at 441 needs -fprofile-instr-generate/-fcoverage-mapping rebuild (run on native amd64).

R3_vulnerable_function_reached.evidence: The freed region at ua_workqueue.c:255 is &sentry->cleanupCallback, enqueued only at removeSession:56 (verbatim in vul source), so removeSession ran. UA_WorkQueue_manuallyProcessDelayed appears in ASan free (#1) and crash (#0) stacks. Patch differential (fix clean) confirms removeSession is the causal site.

R4_vulnerable_line_reached.evidence: ASan free stack frame #1 = ua_workqueue.c:255; source line 255 is `UA_free(dc);`. The freed 368-byte region is the session entry.

R5_sink_reached.evidence: ASan crash frame #0 = ua_workqueue.c:251, heap-use-after-free READ size 8 at 0x613000037240; source line 251 is `SIMPLEQ_FOREACH_SAFE(dc, &wq->delayedCallbacks, next, dc_tmp) {`.

patch_differential.note: The only behavioral change relevant to this PoC is the fix moving synchronous subscription/publish-queue teardown into removeSession before UA_WorkQueue_enqueueDelayed, so the same input no longer leaves a delayed callback referencing freed session memory.

deferred: Tier-B intermediate line coverage (source decode line 441; per-line coverage of removeSession:56) — needs a coverage-instrumented rebuild on native amd64.
Tier-C DFSan taint edge (input bytes -> sink) — the dangling object is a lifetime object rather than a scalar taint value; not run.
